title: Pinned equations for restricted representing data
statement: theorem perfect_hom_open_restricted_data_pinned {I : Type u} [Preorder I] (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone R) {i : I} {Y : Scheme.{u}} (s : Y ⟶ Spec (R.obj i)) [∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))] (B : Y.Opens) (a : derivedPullback B.ι ⊣ schemeDerivedDirectImage B.ι) (Q : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (F : Set.Ici i ⥤ schemeDerivedCategory Y) (d : Cocone F) (h : PerfectHomPushPullData R c s Q F d) (e : PerfectHomOpenRestrictedEquivFields R c s B Q F d) (hs : ∀ j : Set.Ici i, e.stageEquiv j ((schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).obj (F.obj j)) (𝟙 _) = perfectHomOpenRestrictionMap s B (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE j.property))) a (h.stageEquiv j (F.obj j) (𝟙 _))) (hl : e.limitEquiv ((schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).obj d.pt) (𝟙 _) = perfectHomOpenRestrictionMap s B (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) a (h.limitEquiv d.pt (𝟙 _))) : (∀ (j : Set.Ici i) (M : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (f : M ⟶ F.obj j), e.stageEquiv j ((schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).obj M) ((schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).map f) = perfectHomOpenRestrictionMap s B (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE j.property))) a (h.stageEquiv j M f)) ∧ (∀ (M : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (f : M ⟶ d.pt), e.limitEquiv ((schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).obj M) ((schemeMVDerivedRestriction Y B).map f) = perfectHomOpenRestrictionMap s B (Spec.map (c.ι.app i)) a (h.limitEquiv M f))

old_proof.text: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: The planned restriction construction produces a particular compatible representing datum, whereas the Lean statement quantifies over arbitrary hB. Simultaneously negate its stage and apex equivalences: naturality and transition compatibility are preserved, but the asserted equations change sign. With B the full open of Spec(Q), a singleton constant diagram, and the structure sheaf in degree zero, the identity differs from its negative, so the equations cannot hold for both hB choices. No proof of the statement as written is supplied. The existential parent must construct one compatible hB rather than apply this universal assertion.
